item.title: Spin-glass order in a field requires magnetic-field chaos in XY gauge glasses for $d\leq 4$
item.description: arXiv:2611.14109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The XY gauge-glass model is believed to exhibit a spin-glass phase in dimensions $d\geq 3$. In this paper, we prove that, in dimensions $d\leq 4$ and at any finite temperature, a magnetic field applied in a fixed direction, with amplitudes that fluctuate from site to site according to the Rayleigh distribution, must either induce magnetic-field chaos in the spin-glass phase or destroy spin-glass order altogether, whenever a spin-glass phase exists at zero field. In particular, if a spin-glass phase persists under such a field, as predicted by the replica-symmetry-breaking (RSB) picture, it must exhibit magnetic-field chaos. This conclusion follows from our proof that, for any fixed nonzero field strength, the disorder average of the squared overlap between equilibrium spin configurations at zero field and those at nonzero field vanishes in the thermodynamic limit. By gauge transformations, the overlap statistics are identical to the magnetization statistics of an XY gauge glass with correlated bond disorder in a Gaussian random field. Our proof combines this exact identity with quantitative estimates on the suppression of ferromagnetic order by random fields in continuous-spin systems, due to Dario, Harel, and Peled [Commun. Math. Phys. 405, 212 (2024)] and building on the work of Imry and Ma [Phys. Rev. Lett. 35, 1399 (1975)] and of Aizenman and Wehr [Phys. Rev. Lett. 62, 2503 (1989); Commun. Math. Phys. 130, 489 (1990)]. We extend these estimates to bond-dependent interactions. Although our result provides a rare rigorous constraint on the nature of spin-glass phases in finite-dimensional systems, it does not determine whether spin-glass order survives in a field, and therefore does not distinguish between the droplet and RSB pictures. The case of a strictly uniform field remains open.
item.dc:creator: Manaka Okuyama, Masayuki Ohzeki, Hidetoshi Nishimori

item.title: Disorder-Induced Logarithmic Spreading and Localization of Quantum Fluctuations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14200v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Disorder can localize quantum particles, even in the presence of interactions, but its influence on quantum fluctuations beyond mean--field dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the propagation of quantum fluctuations in weakly interacting disordered bosonic systems by comparing the Bose--Hubbard model with the Gross--Pitaevskii equation. We find that, in contrast to ballistic spreading in the disorder--free system, quantum fluctuations exhibit logarithmic spreading at intermediate times under both random and quasiperiodic disorder, before eventually saturating. The spreading rate decreases algebraically with increasing disorder strength, and this behavior persists across different particle numbers and extends to two dimensions. Using a time--dependent Bogoliubov--de Gennes framework, we identify the localized mean--field wavefunction as a time--dependent pairing background that generates quantum fluctuations. The exponential suppression of fluctuation--generation rates with distance provides a physical mechanism for the logarithmically advancing fluctuation front. Our results reveal a distinct regime of disorder--controlled quantum--fluctuation dynamics and establish disorder as a means of controlling their spreading.
item.dc:creator: Ang Yang, Jingxuan Zhang, Lei Ying

item.title: Surface codes with coherent errors: optimal decoding and finite-size crossovers
item.description: arXiv:2611.13098v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the surface code under uniform coherent $Z$ rotations $\exp{(i\theta Z)}$ followed by perfect syndrome measurements, a setting known to exhibit strong finite-size effects that complicate the extraction of the asymptotic decoding threshold. We identify finite-size behavior of both Pauli decoding measures and the coherent information with two characteristic lengths: an algebraic ballistic-crossover scale $d_{\mathrm{ba}}\sim 1/\beta_R^{\alpha}$ ($\alpha=1$ for odd $d$ and $\alpha=2$ for even $d$) and a much larger renormalization-group scale $d_\mathrm{RG}\sim \exp{(C/\beta^{4}_R)}$, where $\beta_R=-\tfrac{1}{2}\ln\tan\theta$ and $d$ is the system size. As $\theta$ approaches the ballistic SWAP point $\pi/4$, the two length scales diverge at very different rates, leaving a broad intermediate regime $d_{\mathrm{ba}}\ll d\ll d_\mathrm{RG}$ in which these quantities show substantial finite-size drift and approximate plateaus. To establish the microscopic basis of this crossover picture, we derive a leading inter-flavor quartic interaction of order $\beta_R^2$ in the replicated Majorana theory, which provides a route to the class-D nonlinear sigma model. The resulting marginal RG flow motivates the scaling variable $X_4=\beta_R^4\ln d$, in which free-fermion simulations show approximate collapse of decoding measures. These results are consistent with a Pauli-decoding threshold at $\theta_c=\pi/4$ in the thermodynamic limit. For any even $d$, we prove that maximum-likelihood Pauli decoding maximizes entanglement fidelity over all deterministic syndrome-conditioned quantum recoveries, and that its decoding threshold attains the quantum-optimal limit, coinciding with the one defined by coherent information.
item.dc:creator: Xu-Dong Dai, Zhou-Quan Wan, Xi Dai, Guo-Yi Zhu

item.title: Everything in its right place: attention is a radio head
item.description: arXiv:2611.13146v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Attention, the core of language models, is a digital calculation over tokens: an exponential selects them, a division normalizes and a positional code sets the order. We show that attention can instead emerge from the synchronization of a receiver with its context tokens. Each past token is an oscillator whose state carries its content and whose frequency drifts with its age. The present token selects them by content, aligning an antenna with its query, and by position, setting the frequency of a receiver with its dial. Solving Kuramoto's problem for this receiver yields an attention layer in closed form with two phases: above a critical coupling set by the context, the receiver locks and its weights normalize; below it, it stays silent and its weights sum to less than one. Trained networks use both phases to select, abstain and count, fail where the theory predicts and keep reading far beyond the training length. Each part of attention finds its place in one device, a radio head: it tunes in to what to hear and when, and stays silent when nothing relevant is on air.
item.dc:creator: Llu\'is Arola-Fern\'andez, Aissam Khadraoui, Alex Arenas

item.title: Pair localization in one-dimensional quasicrystals with spin-dependent hopping
item.description: arXiv:2611.13553v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the quantum localization of two interacting particles moving in a one-dimensional quasicrystal with unequal hopping amplitudes. Using a two-body Green's function approach, we determine the localization phase diagram of attractively and repulsively bound pairs, showing that increasing the hopping amplitude of one constituent while keeping the other fixed raises the critical quasiperiodic strength, promoting pair delocalization. The localization threshold nevertheless remains bounded above by the Aubry-Andr\'e critical point of the slower constituent. Effective analytical descriptions capture pair localization in the limits of strong hopping imbalance and strong interactions. The dynamics of an initially on-site pair provides signatures of delocalization induced by unequal hopping amplitudes. In particular, the effective spreading exponent of the root-mean-square width of a pair distribution reveals a progression from localized to subdiffusive and eventually superdiffusive behavior as the hopping ratio increases. Our results establish unequal hopping amplitudes as a means of tuning the transport properties of interacting pairs in quasiperiodic lattices, with direct relevance to ultracold atoms in optical lattices.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Rosas, U. A. D\'iaz-Reynoso, Francisco Mireles, G. A. Dom\'inguez-Castro

item.title: Non-Gaussian limit distributions of giant-component sizes in inhomogeneous networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.13683v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We demonstrate that the size distribution of giant components in percolation and epidemic spreading models on highly inhomogeneous networks often fails to converge to a Gaussian distribution in the thermodynamic limit. Instead, when appropriately scaled, the distribution converges to a non-Gaussian limit distribution (NGLD). This scaling behavior aligns with the generalized central limit theorem (GCLT), which governs sums of random variables following heavy-tailed distributions. For scale-free networks, the scaling exponent is determined solely by the degree exponent of the network, independently of the control parameter. In contrast, on the Farey graph, a deterministic hierarchical small-world network, the scaling exponent varies continuously with the control parameter.
item.dc:creator: Tomoaki Nogawa, Takehisa Hasegawa

item.title: Universal Multichannel Coherence-Mediated Thermal Transport in Carbon Allotropes: Experimental Evidence and Scaling Laws
item.description: arXiv:2611.14165v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Understanding thermal transport in structurally disordered carbon materials remains a fundamental challenge because conventional models based on a single coherence contribution cannot accurately describe heat conduction over a broad temperature range. In this work, the thermal conductivity of graphene oxide (GO), thermally reduced graphene oxide (trGO), GO-hydrated fullerene composites (GO-HyFn), expanded graphite (EG), and EG-multiwalled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) composites was measured between 4.5 and 300 K. Despite substantial differences in density, porosity, graphitic ordering, and microstructure, all materials exhibit glass-like temperature dependence of thermal conductivity. The experimental results demonstrate that the conventional two-channel model, comprising a Peierls contribution and a single thermally activated coherence term, systematically fails to reproduce the observed temperature dependence. To resolve this discrepancy, we propose a generalized multichannel phenomenological model in which the coherence contribution consists of up to three Arrhenius-type channels with distinct activation energies. Depending on the structural state, two or three coherence channels are required to accurately describe the thermal conductivity. A key finding is the reproducible hierarchy of activation energies across diverse carbon allotropes, following approximately (E2 ~ 4E1 and E3 ~ (12-25)E1). While the channel amplitudes increase with material density, the activation energies remain nearly invariant, indicating universal vibrational energy scales. The proposed framework also consistently describes published data for other disordered carbon materials. These results provide experimental evidence for multichannel coherence-mediated heat transport and establish a unified phenomenological bridge between structural hierarchy with thermal transport in disordered carbon solids.
item.dc:creator: A. Je\.{z}owski, A. I. Krivchikov, O. A. Korolyuk, V. V. Sagan, Y. V. Horbatenko, S. V. Cherednychenko, A. V. Dolbin, N. A. Vinnikov, O. Bezkrovnyi, D. Szewczyk

item.title: Stagewise and interpretable emergence of inside-outside computation in Transformer-based language models
item.description: arXiv:2611.14221v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Variability in syntactic structure and parsing ambiguity are fundamental aspects of natural language which modern LLMs have to learn to deal with proficiently. Previous "post-mortem" studies have shown that fully trained Transformers indeed approximate canonical parsing algorithms such as inside-outside, but little is established theoretically about how this is actually learned. Here, we make a first step towards addressing this by studying the learning dynamics in synthetic context-free grammars with variable parse tree topology. The stagewise learning curves are fully interpretable, in the sense that all of the loss stages a) can be computed analytically, and b) can be clearly associated to the representation of a hidden latent tree variable, which allows to lift ambiguity and utilize information from wider contexts. By probing representations, we visualize the emergence of inside-outside computation across depth and during training: while during early stages local (bigram/trigram) information is used and involves only a few initial layers, gradually the Transformer develops an encoder-decoder structure where the most abstract latent information is encoded in the middle, and the latter half of the network is used to progressively refine the final token prediction. This organization of computation is reminiscent of findings in real-world LLMs, and importantly applies here to a synthetic model which allows full analytical control of the data statistics, thus opening the door to theoretical progress.
item.dc:creator: Jack T. Parley

item.title: Anomalous Localization and Mobility Edges in Non-Hermitian Quasicrystals with Disordered Imaginary Gauge Fields
item.description: arXiv:2601.14754v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: How localization emerges in open wave systems can differ fundamentally from the familiar picture in closed materials. Here we show that a quasiperiodic chain with spatially disordered non-reciprocal couplings supports a form of localization in which the relevant boundary does not separate spreading and trapped waves, but two different kinds of confinement. One regime shows erratic skin accumulation at disorder-selected positions inside the lattice, whereas the other shows conventional Anderson localization with centers distributed across the system. Adding longer-range hopping turns this transition into an anomalous mobility edge between these two localized sectors. We identify the transition using real-space profiles, Lyapunov exponents, spectral winding, and wave-packet evolution. For individual disorder realizations, wave packets drift in a direction fixed by spectral topology, while averaging over disorder cancels opposite drifts and restores conventional transport. These results provide experimentally accessible signatures of anomalous localization in engineered open systems.
item.dc:creator: Guolin Nan, Zhijian Li, Feng Mei, Zhihao Xu

item.title: Floquet mobility edges and transport in a periodically driven generalized Aubry-Andr\'e model
item.description: arXiv:2604.21992v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the effect of a periodic electric field drive on the generalized Aubry-Andr\'e model, also known as the Ganeshan-Pixley-Das Sarma (GPD) model, which is well known as a host of mobility edges. Our study of the Floquet spectrum of the driven GPD model uncovers the emergence of two distinct Floquet mobility edges, a delocalized--localized (DL) edge in the bounded regime, and a multifractal--localized (ML) edge in the unbounded regime. By mapping the high-frequency effective Hamiltonian to the static GPD model via a Bessel-renormalized hopping, the driven mobility edge formulae follow directly, with drive-induced localization arising naturally at specific values of the driving parameters, where the effective tunneling is coherently suppressed. Combined with numerical diagnostics such as the fractal dimension and inverse participation ratio, we demonstrate that these mobility edges can be effectively controlled by the amplitude and frequency of the electric field drive. Furthermore, the dynamical study of the periodically driven GPD model demonstrates superdiffusive to almost ballistic transport in the bounded regime corresponding to the DL edges, whereas subdiffusive transport is observed in the unbounded regime associated with the ML edges. We also analyze deviations from the high-frequency effective description by explicitly examining the low-frequency driving regime, where significant and counterintuitive deviations in both spectral properties and transport behavior are observed. Our study highlights the interplay of a quasiperiodic potential and a periodically varying electric field drive as a powerful mechanism to engineer mobility edges and control transport in systems with rich spectral features.
item.dc:creator: Jayashis Das, Vatsana Tiwari, Manish Kumar, Auditya Sharma

item.title: Linear equivalence of nonlinear recurrent neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2604.23489v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The covariance matrix of a large nonlinear recurrent neural network is shown to match that of a linear network with the same couplings, driven by independent noise, for typical random couplings with independent, identically distributed elements. This linear equivalence, previously proposed as an ansatz, is derived using a two-site cavity method and confirmed in simulations. With zero mean activities, and with sign-flip symmetry when units repeat, weak correlations between units reduce even-order moments at leading order to products of single-site and two-site moments, recovering results first obtained diagrammatically. In models with nonzero mean activities, including a recurrent network with Hebbian plasticity and a saturating Lotka-Volterra model, the temporal means obey a self-consistent mean-field equation, and linear equivalence holds for the connected covariance matrix. Parts of this work were done in collaboration with AI models.
item.dc:creator: David G. Clark

item.title: Semi-fractality and localization on a chiral Cayley tree
item.description: arXiv:2607.18179v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a quantum particle hopping on an infinite Cayley tree with nearest-neighbor hopping amplitudes drawn from a distribution singular as $|t|^{-a}$ near weak links and no on-site disorder. Because the graph is bipartite, the model has chiral symmetry, which strongly affects the statistics of eigenstates at the center of the spectrum. We derive the two power-law tail exponents of the local-density-of-states distribution from the band-center cavity equation and compare the predictions with population dynamics. These tails imply an unusual form of wave-function statistics, which we call semi-fractality: the eigenstates occupy an extensive fraction of the system, but their higher moments behave as in a multifractal state. We find that the symmetry properties of the local-density-of-states distribution are not fixed only by the symmetry class, but vary continuously with the exponent controlling the power-law hopping distribution. As this exponent is changed, the system crosses from a semi-fractal regime to a localized one. At the transition, the wave functions realize an extreme intermediate form that we call semi-localized, simultaneously extended in their support but localized according to higher moments.
item.dc:creator: Carlo Vanoni, Vladimir E. Kravtsov, Aleksey V. Lunkin, Boris L. Altshuler

item.title: Dynamic Pseudogap Model
item.description: arXiv:2608.19592v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We formulate a theory of pseudogap formation generated by dynamic finite nesting vector ${\bf Q}$ fluctuations with characteristic oscillation frequency $\omega_0$, and damping $\gamma$. Starting from a Hamiltonian describing electrons coupled to a classical Gaussian random field, we introduce the double - series representations of the single - particle Green's function within an Abelian (commuting) approximation to the exact SU(2) time evolution of the pseudogap problem. The resulting propagator naturally acquires a generalized Bogoliubov structure in which every stochastic scattering history is characterized by an effective dynamic gap, leading to a coherent superposition of dynamically broadened sidebands with complex Poisson weights. A central result of the theory is the emergence of a dynamically generated decoherence scale $\Gamma_{\rm eff}$ governing the crossover between two qualitatively different pseudogap regimes. For $\omega_0>\Gamma_{\rm eff}$ the fluctuating field is resolved coherently and the double-series representation provides a controlled description of dynamic sideband formation. Conversely, when $\Gamma_{\rm eff}\gtrsim\omega_0$, coherence is progressively lost and the theory crosses over to the quasistatic fluctuating - gap regime described by the exact continued-fraction solution. The coherent and quasistatic descriptions are therefore interpreted as two complementary asymptotic limits of the same microscopic dynamic pseudogap model. The detailed results of numerical calculations for electron spectral density and density of states supporting our approach are presented for different sets of model parameters confirming the general picture of this crossover.
item.dc:creator: E. Z. Kuchinskii, M. V. Sadovskii

item.title: Lyapunov spectrum scaling transition for quasiperiodic nonlinear unitaries
item.description: arXiv:2607.14549v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the Lyapunov spectrum scaling of thermal weakly-nonlinear unitary maps in the presence of quasiperiodic potentials. We search for the crossover from long-range to short-range scaling as the localization length {\xi} decreases and compare the details to the case of uncorrelated Anderson disorder [Phys. Rev. Res. 6 L012064 (2024)]. A comparative statistical analysis of the eigenstates for the linear case shows that quasiperiodicity has a stronger localization impact at the same value of {\xi}. Therefore we expect that the scaling crossover should be enhanced as well. However, the numerical analysis shows that it is strongly delayed as compared to Anderson disorder, and is observed at anomalously small values of {\xi}. These findings hint at the potential impact of long range correlations of quasiperiodic localized eigenstates, which persist in the presence of interactions even in the case of integrability breaking and thermalization.
item.dc:creator: Xiaodong Zhang, Barbara Dietz, Sergej Flach

item.title: Negative-Power Density of States in Chiral-Orthogonal Disordered Systems and the IR Phase of QCD
item.description: arXiv:2610.35524v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The recently discovered IR phase of QCD is characterized by an infrared (IR) sector of Dirac modes that separates and dynamically decouples from the bulk of the spectrum, becoming scale invariant in the process [1]. Among key features of this IR sector is the negative power-law behavior of Dirac spectral density near zero with power close to $-1$. Here we start investigating to what extent can this behavior be mimicked by chiral Anderson models. In particular, we study 3-D chiral-orthogonal systems with logarithmic off-diagonal disorder where negative-power ``spikes'' have been observed [2]. We find that for disorders of moderate strength $W$, these models in fact do not have a power-singular density of states (DOS) at zero energy in the thermodynamic limit. Rather, the corresponding power vanishes but the spectrum features a very accurate negative-power behavior on an interval around $E=1$, spreading increasingly closer to $E=0$ and $E=\infty$ with increasing $W$. We connect this to the fact that random hoppings $t$ in these quantum systems are drawn from a scale-invariant $1/t$ distribution regularized via $t \in [e^{-W/2}, e^{W/2}]$, and DOS with negative power can naturally arise inside that range. In fact, we find that power $p$ in the vicinity of energy $E$ satisfies $\lim_{W \to \infty} p(W, E) = -1$ for all $E$ we access. This indicates that, upon removing the cutoff $W$, quantum mechanics transforms the scale-invariant $1/t$ noise into a scale-invariant $1/E$ distribution of eigenstates, which mimics the interpretation of scale-invariant Dirac spectral densities in the IR phase as being due to scale-invariant glue backgrounds [1]. Our results imply that, when modeling the IR phase, the IR cutoff in chiral Anderson systems needs to be tied to their randomness strength $W$ rather than to their lattice size $L$.
item.dc:creator: Ji\v{r}\'i Adam, Jr., Andrei Alexandru, Navdeep Singh Dhindsa, Ivan Horv\'ath, Frank X. Lee, Nilmani Mathur
